## What's new
## Changed
## Fixed
- Prevented Input Dock from recursively wrapping zsh line-editor hooks when shell plugins use `add-zle-hook-widget`.

## What's new
- Added SGR-pixel mouse reporting for applications that request precise device-pixel coordinates. - Added the VS Code-compatible Palenight palette and kept the previous palette as Palenight Dark. - Added active Python virtual-environment names to the session status bar when zsh uses the Input Dock. - Added an option to disable scroll smoothing for compatibility with external scrolling utilities such as Mos. - Added a native context menu to the normal terminal surface for copying, pasting, splitting panes, and clearing the buffer. ## Changed
- Removed command-output block folding, its keyboard shortcut, and its Motion setting. - Replaced Commit and New line effects with one Buffer lift control offering Off, the original Smooth motion, and the former Snap motion as Spring. - Combined the status bar motion controls into one switch with Odometer counter animation. - Made Shift-click and plain Shift-arrow keys extend or shrink terminal selections from their fixed edge. - Made cold starts show the terminal window and its stable input dock substantially faster. - Made new tabs appear immediately while their shell and integration are prepared off the UI thread. - Reduced typing latency by sending ready terminal input immediately. - Cut multi-tab memory use by releasing full-size Metal drawable buffers for inactive tabs.
## Fixed
- Reset terminal modes and live metadata completely while preserving MetalTerm scrollback and terminal color overrides. - Handled complete G0–G3 character-set designation sequences without increasing terminal memory use. - Matched reverse-wrap behavior for backspace and backward cursor movement across lines. - Kept terminal content, cursor placement, wrapping, and synchronized output stable through window resizes. - Made mouse tracking honor the latest requested event level while keeping mode queries accurate. - Restored complete cursor state across save/restore sequences and alternate-screen transitions. - Preserved complex Unicode grapheme clusters—including long combining sequences, emoji variation selectors, and ZWJ emoji—across streamed terminal input, terminal controls, resizes, and screen switches.

## What's new
- Added an opt-in setting that lets macOS restore terminal windows to their previous Spaces after login. - Added confirmation before closing panes, tabs, windows, or the app when a foreground process is running or a window contains multiple tabs, with configurable never, running, and always modes. - Made files and folders in focused terminal windows openable with ⌘-click, including bare `ls` names, paths with spaces, and historical relative paths. - Added right-aligned execution times and a smoothly animated live command status with a soft fade-in and an adjustable display threshold in Settings. - Added adjustable macOS background blur that follows Reduce Transparency and stays off for fully opaque windows, plus control over whether window opacity includes the header and status bars.
## Changed
## Fixed
- Cleared terminal selections with Escape, typed input, ordinary navigation keys, and IME composition while preserving keyboard selection and each key's normal terminal action. - Cleared the query and all match highlights whenever Find is closed. - Kept terminal history continuous during animated multi-line and repeated output instead of briefly opening a blank band at the top of the window. - Made trackpad and precise-mouse history scrolling update smoothly at the display refresh rate, settle consistently at the live bottom, stop promptly after momentum ends, and restore zero-frame idle.
